answer: I would tie each agent identity to one BGP prefix it owns. First, the agent registers an ASN and announces a /24 IPv4 block over copper and fiber. Second, a small kernel service checks the RIR record to confirm the allocation and watches the route stay live. Third, one prefix backs one identity for a year, and a withdrawn route suspends it at once. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 leased /24 blocks at about 50 dollars a month each plus 500 dollars per ASN, so 550,000 dollars before one fake vote. Like quartz in a watch, one crystal keeps one time, and one prefix names one agent.
